subject: Request: handback playbook & latency attribution for private deployment
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hydroworks.io>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Sanjay Patel <sanjay.patel@hydroworks.io>, procurement@hydroworks.io
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: handback playbook & latency attribution for private deployment

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. We're getting ready to finalize the Private deployment and have a couple of outstanding asks from our ops and security teams before we sign the final SOW. TL;DR: Hydroworks is asking Redwood to accept a narrow "handback" process that attributes tail latency in our on-prem edge to our infra for a limited set of failure modes, and to provide a one-page operational playbook describing exactly where Redwood's observability ends and Hydroworks' responsibility begins.

Specifically we need:
- A short playbook (runbook) that the Hydroworks NOC can follow to triage latency spikes and to confirm when the root cause is on our side (e.g., WAN jitter, customer NAT device, our firewall or peering).
- A precise list of telemetry Redwood requires (tcpdump/traceroute windows, sample logs, and request IDs) and retention window for evidence collection.
- A proposed temporary SLO adjustment for the first 90 days of go-live in the event we see repeated short (100–500ms) tail events originating from our edge. We understand Redwood's baseline SLOs; asking for a scoped exception with rollback triggers.

I've attached a simple topology diagram showing our network handoff to Redwood's VPC (hydroworks_topology.pdf). Our legal team asked me to confirm this will be captured as an appendix rather than an SLA blanket waiver.

Appreciate any draft playbook or a checklist you can send by early next week so we can loop in our security folks.

Best,
Liam
Head of Infrastructure, Hydroworks

---
Attachment: hydroworks_topology.pdf (1 page PDF)

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@hydroworks.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, contracts@hydroworks.io
Date: Fri, 30 Jun 2028 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: handback playbook & latency attribution for private deployment

Hi Liam — thanks for the clear summary and the topology diagram. We're glad Hydroworks is being proactive here. A few quick points and a plan for next steps: 

1) Scope — Redwood is open to a documented handback/playbook approach limited to customer-controlled network elements (WAN, on-prem firewall/NAT, edge router) where the evidence incontrovertibly shows the issue originated on the customer side. We will not accept a broad SLA waiver; exceptions must be time-boxed and tied to observable signals.

2) Telemetry — we need: request_id, ingress timestamp, egress timestamp, backend hop timings, and a 10s packet capture window around the spike (pcap). Retention: 30 days for troubleshooting by default; longer only by explicit request.

3) Temporary SLO adjustment — we can propose a 90-day monitoring window where Redwood's latency SLO on the affected route is adjusted from 99.9% < 200ms to 99.5% < 250ms for the first 90 days, with automatic reversion unless agreed to extend via a PRR (post-incident review). We also want clear rollback triggers (e.g., 3 incidents > 200ms attributable to customer infra within a 30-day window).

Next steps: I'll get Karthik to draft a short "handback playbook" and a proposed appendix that pins the evidence types and the rollback triggers. Can you confirm whether Hydroworks' security team requires specific legal language (they mentioned an appendix vs. amendment)? If you can put that in writing we'll make sure the draft aligns.

I'll aim to circulate a first draft by Monday EOD.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

Subject: Draft: handback playbook and appendix (internal)

Kim / Tessa — attaching an internal draft of the handback playbook and appendix language (redwood_handback_playbook_draft.md). Key items I recommend we include in the customer-facing version: 

- Definition of "customer-controlled network elements" (explicit list).
- Exact telemetry schema (json) with example traceroute output and request_id mapping.
- A 7-step triage checklist for the customer NOC with outcome buckets: (customer-resolved / joint-triage / Redwood-resolved).
- Timebox: 90-day provisional SLO with automated rollback after 90 days unless extended by mutual written agreement.
- Evidence rules: pcap + traceroute + Router control-plane logs OR BGP route change trace. Any single item alone is not sufficient.

I've marked language that looks like a waiver — we'll convert those to "handback" language and reference a DocuSign appendix instead of changing the master SLA.

Recommend we also offer a 30-day onboarding window where Redwood will provide a named on-call for 24/7 escalation (included as part of the Dedicated onboarding credits).

I'll send the cleaned customer copy once you approve.

— Karthik
Sr. Product Manager, Reliability
